model_rules.two_gates: Gate 1 decides whether an artifact EXISTS for a viewer (component 13, audience). Gate 2 decides which ROWS a viewer sees inside it (component 12, data scope). They are independent: a viewer can be correctly entitled and correctly see zero rows.
model_rules.counts_are_computed: Every count on this screen — "sees 8 of 60" — is derived from the roster at paint time. No count is stored. A stated count stops being true the moment the roster changes and nothing notices.
model_rules.rule_shape: A person is full-scope, or restricted by exactly one BASIS field plus the values of it they may see. A separate boolean mask hides row-level money while leaving totals visible.
model_rules.legal_basis: A field qualifies as a restriction basis only if every one of its values maps to a definite, non-empty set of the roster. Continuous measures — forecast, EAC variance, percent complete — are excluded: a rule on them re-resolves every week, which makes it a filter, not an access rule.
model_rules.no_approval: There is no approval queue. Publishing, granting and revoking are immediate and logged. (Superseded the earlier CAPEX draft, which carried a six-item approval queue.)
model_rules.admin_holds_none: The platform administrator administers entitlement and does not thereby acquire it. Their zero scope is by design, not omission.
model_rules.publishing_never_widens: Adding a reader to an artifact grants existence, never rows. The reader opens it under their own rule.

gate1.question: May this viewer see that this report EXISTS?
gate1.saysNothingAbout: which rows a viewer's predicate admits

gate2.question: Which rows does this viewer's predicate ADMIT?
gate2.shape: a predicate with a digest, resolved once per session
gate2.cannotBeFrontEnd: If the browser receives 60 rows and shows 8, the viewer has 60. Every dev-tools session would be a full-portfolio export. This is why the renderer rule forbids filtering in the browser.

two_gates.neverCollapse: The two are administered in two separate grids. A viewer can be entitled to a report and still see zero rows, and that is a correct outcome -- not an error.
twelveObligations: Expose a resolved scope predicate as a first-class SESSION artifact with a digest, not a role lookup at query time. A digest is what makes an audit possible.
Define scope CLASSES as an administrable concept. Per-user predicates do not survive the tenth user.
two_gates.prototypeStance: Read-only in three places -- login, govern (scope class column), trace (predicate digest per entry). NO Gate 2 editor: 12 is a stub and a convincing editor would settle an unreviewed design (PD-21).

declaredAggregate.question: May this viewer read a figure DECLARED over a population wider than their predicate admits?
declaredAggregate.rule: A block whose source is a declared aggregate (`portfolio` and its sub-objects) requires an unrestricted predicate. Any narrower predicate means the published figure covers rows the viewer may not read.
declaredAggregate.neverSubstitute: Never re-aggregate the admitted rows under the declared figure's label. The sample of 60 projects is 12.7% of a 612-project programme and its quarterly variance has the opposite sign, so a re-aggregation is not a smaller version of the same answer -- it is a different answer wearing its name.
declaredAggregate.renders: You are entitled to this report. It publishes portfolio figures declared over the whole programme, and your data scope admits a subset of it, so those figures are not shown. This is the scope working, not a query returning nothing.
declaredAggregate.aggregateGrainIsNotThis: A scope class at `aggregate` grain has an unrestricted predicate and IS served these figures -- it just gets no detail rows. The two outcomes look similar on screen and have opposite causes.

gate_1_audience_entitlement.note: Audience entitlement (gate 1) -- who may see that a report EXISTS. It says nothing about which rows a viewer's predicate admits; that is gate 2 below. A viewer can be entitled to a report and correctly see zero rows in it.

legend.b: entitled once published -- blocked at validation
legend.a: entitled -- archived, opens by link only

gate_1_audience_entitlement.legendNote: p and b are not entitlement states. The persona is in the audience; the report is not servable yet. Rendering them as 'entitled' would tell an admin the audience was live when nothing has been published. 'a' is the opposite case and the one most easily got wrong: an archived report is fully servable and the persona is fully entitled -- what archiving removed is discovery, not access. A link to it in a filing, a ticket or an email must still open. Showing it as 'not entitled' would tell an admin to go looking for a permissions problem that does not exist.
gate_1_audience_entitlement.adminNote: The Platform Admin row is 'n' across every report by design. An admin administers entitlement without holding it -- an admin exception in the presentation layer is how admin backdoors get built.

gate_2_data_scope.note: Data scope (gate 2) -- which rows a session's predicate admits and which columns are masked. Resolved once per session at the e_project node, applied server-side, and sealed into every trace as a digest of the predicate text.

rows.label: Aggregate only
rows.note: Not assigned to any persona in this fixture. Retained because the class taxonomy is the point, and a class with no current holder is normal.
rows.unassignedNote: Defined and held by nobody. It exists so the shape is designed before the first customer needs it, not invented under time pressure when they do.

rows.label: Metadata only
rows.note: Platform Admin. Sees structure, lineage, cost and access -- no figures. An admin exception in the presentation layer is how admin backdoors get built, so the predicate is FALSE at the server and there is no override anywhere.

gate_2_data_scope.serverSideNote: The predicate is applied in the query, not filtered out of a result set on the way to the screen. A client-side scope filter is a scope that leaks the moment anyone reads the network tab.
gate_2_data_scope.unassignedNote: Aggregate-only is defined and unassigned -- it exists so the aggregate-grain path is exercised before a customer needs it. An unassigned class is shown as unassigned, not hidden.
gate_2_data_scope.digestNote: Digests are computed at session resolution from the predicate text. The fixture carries the value a trace displays; 20_api.js must recompute it, or the digest proves nothing it claims to prove.

retained_but_not_displayed.why: The ported screen shows the governance the demo has to be able to DO — resolve a rule, grant a reader, revoke a publication, read the log. These are governance the demo has to be able to SHOW a reviewer, and the React frontend renders them from this file. They stay in the data even though the HTML no longer draws them; dropping them because a screen stopped rendering them would be a silent deletion.
retained_but_not_displayed.divergence: The gate grids are persona-shaped (five personas x three reports) while the screen is email-shaped. Same five people; the grids predate the email-only audience decision of August 13, 2026 and are kept as the reviewer-facing matrix view.

dropped_from_the_previous_build.why: The screen this package now mirrors has no approval step, and the August 13 2026 access design removed it deliberately: publishing, granting and revoking are immediate and logged. Keeping the queue in the data would reintroduce the contradiction the memo used to record as an open conflict. It is resolved in favour of no approval.
